# How matching ranks and excludes people

<!-- Generated by scripts/render-matching-rules.ts from src/modules/matching/domain/matching-rules.ts. Do not edit by hand: a test fails when this file and the code disagree. -->

Matching answers one question for one shift: **who could work it, in what order, and why not the others.** This is the whole rule. It is the same for every facility, it does not learn, and nothing in it is chosen by hand for a particular person.

## When a match runs, and who is looked at

- **Only when somebody at the facility asks for one.** Nothing runs a match on its own, and a match offers nobody anything: it ranks, a person decides whom to invite.
- **Only for work that can be offered.** The request must be published, its shift must not have started, and the facility must be verified and in date. Anything else is refused and leaves no record.
- **The pool is everybody registered in the request’s profession**, except anybody who has withdrawn either consent matching rests on: letting facilities see their profile, or sharing their credentials with a facility. They are left out altogether: not ranked, not listed as excluded and not counted.
- **Everybody in the pool is then either excluded, with every reason that applies, or ranked.**

## Who is excluded

A person is excluded if **any** of these applies. All the reasons that apply are recorded, not only the first, so that “why did nobody match?” has a whole answer.

| Reason | About | Applies when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `category_mismatch` | the shift | Their profession is not the one the request asks for. The pool is already limited to the request’s profession, so this is a second check behind that filter. |
| `specialty_mismatch` | the shift | The request names a specialty and theirs is different or not recorded. A request that names none accepts any. |
| `level_mismatch` | the shift | The request names a level and the level recorded against their registration is different, or none has been recorded. Nobody is assumed to be at a level nobody recorded for them. A request that names none accepts any. |
| `supervision_required` | the shift | Their registration category says they work under supervision and the shift does not say anybody is there to supervise them. |
| `not_eligible` | the person | They do not pass the eligibility rule: an account that can be used, a profile, a verified identity that matches their name, an active registration checked recently enough, every credential the profession requires, and a clear screening. The rule is one function, `isEligibleForMatching`, called here and not restated. |
| `unavailable` | their time | They have not offered the whole shift: no availability they set covers it from its start to its end, or they have offered none. |
| `blocked` | their time | A period they blocked (leave, training, away) overlaps any part of the shift. This is checked before availability, so somebody who is blocked and has also offered nothing is reported as blocked, not unavailable. |
| `already_assigned` | their time | They hold a confirmed assignment that overlaps any part of the shift. A cancelled one does not count. |
| `travel_preference` | their wishes | Their own travel preference rules the shift out: “same local government area” and the facility is in another, or “same state” and the facility is in another state. “Anywhere” never excludes. |

A facility is shown the reasons but not whose they are: whose diary is full is that person’s business. A practitioner who is ranked is shown to the facility by initials only, with no phone number, until a booking exists.

## How the rest are ranked

Each person who is not excluded scores out of 100 on four factors. The weights are fixed in the code, not in a settings table, so that a ranking cannot change because somebody edited a row, and the same inputs always give the same ranking.

| Factor | Recorded as | Points available |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Experience | `experience` | 30 |
| Nearness | `proximity` | 35 |
| Rest | `fatigue` | 20 |
| Reliability | `reliability` | 15 |
| **Total** | | **100** |

### Experience (30 points)

The years of experience on their profile, counted up to 10 and no further, as a share of 10. More than 10 years does not make somebody more suitable for one shift, and left uncapped it would put a veteran far away ahead of somebody next door who is rested and free. 0 years scores 0; 2 years scores 0.2; 5 years scores 0.5; 10 years scores 1; 25 years scores 1.

### Nearness (35 points)

Where the facility is relative to the practitioner’s home, in three steps, because nothing in the system holds a distance:

- their home is in the same local government area as the facility: **1**
- their home is in the same state: **0.6**
- their home is in another state, or they have not said where they live: **0.2**

Somebody who has not said where they live counts as far away. A guess in their favour would put them ahead of somebody who is nearby.

### Rest (20 points)

The hours of assignments that are still confirmed and start in the 7 days before this shift starts, each counted in full. None is full marks, 48 or more is nothing, and it falls in a straight line between. 0 hours scores 1; 12 hours scores 0.75; 24 hours scores 0.5; 48 hours scores 0; 68 hours scores 0. A shift already worked and approved is marked completed and is **not counted today**, and neither is a cancelled one or an offer not yet accepted, so for a shift at short notice this factor can flatter somebody who has just worked a heavy week.

### Reliability (15 points)

The share of their decided shifts that they worked: shifts completed, divided by shifts completed plus shifts they did not honour where a person decided the fault was theirs. An excused absence, a shift the facility cancelled and one still to be worked are in neither number, so an excusal can never lower the score. Until 5 assignments are completed everybody scores 0.5, in the middle: no history is not evidence of unreliability, and a newcomer and an average practitioner rank alike on this factor. After that, a completed share of 0.5 scores 0.5; a completed share of 0.8 scores 0.8; a completed share of 1 scores 1.

## The order, and ties

The score is the four factors’ points added up. Each factor’s points and the total are rounded to two decimal places before anybody is compared, so two people whose scores are equal to two places are tied. A tie goes to the lower user id, which is arbitrary but never different from one run to the next. Ranks run 1, 2, 3 with no gaps. The people left out are listed in user id order.

## A worked example

Six practitioners for one shift that asks for nothing beyond the profession:

- **A**: 8 years, same local government area, 12 hours committed this week, 9 of the 10 shifts decided were worked.
- **B**: 3 years, same state, nothing committed, a newcomer with 2 shifts done.
- **C**: 12 years, another state, 40 hours committed, 20 shifts done and all worked.
- **D**: identical to E in everything the engine looks at.
- **E**: identical to D in everything the engine looks at.
- **F**: not yet through eligibility, and blocked on that day.

What the engine makes of them:

| Rank | Candidate | Experience | Nearness | Rest | Reliability | Score |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | A | 24 | 35 | 15 | 13.5 | **87.5** |
| 2 | D | 15 | 21 | 20 | 7.5 | **63.5** |
| 3 | E | 15 | 21 | 20 | 7.5 | **63.5** |
| 4 | B | 9 | 21 | 20 | 7.5 | **57.5** |
| 5 | C | 30 | 7 | 3.33 | 15 | **55.33** |

Left out, with every reason that applied:

- F: `not_eligible`, `blocked`

D and E are tied on 63.5, so D, the lower id, is ranked first. C has the most experience and the best record of anybody ranked and still comes last, because nearness and rest carry 55 of the 100 points.

## What is kept

Every run is stored with the weights that produced it, every ranked person’s points under each factor, and every excluded person’s reasons. A ranking that nobody can look at again explains nothing, and without the weights an old run could not be read once they changed.

## What it does not do

- **It does not look at competencies.** Level and supervision are hard filters; individual competencies are not built.
- **It does not count shifts already worked toward rest.** Only assignments still confirmed are added up, so a week of shifts that have been approved no longer weighs on the next shift’s ranking.
- **It does not measure distance.** Nearness is the three steps above until the system holds where people and facilities are.
- **It does not use pay, a facility’s preferences or who was offered the last shift.** A facility cannot move one person up.
- **It does not learn.** Reliability uses decided outcomes only, as above.

## Changing a rule

A weight, a cap or a filter is a change to `src/modules/matching/domain/engine.ts`, with a review and a new snapshot, and then to this page: edit `matching-rules.ts`, run `pnpm tsx scripts/render-matching-rules.ts`, and commit both. The tests refuse a page that disagrees with the engine.
